items.why: The report measures flake 2 at "1368.99 ± 0.23 cm-1, FWHM 21.6" against flake 1 at "1366.19", a shift of "+2.84 ± 0.25 cm-1", and says it "fits a few-layer or monolayer flake on SiO2/Si".
It gives the size of the shift ("Gorbachev reports 1L shifted up 2-4 cm-1") and says "position is not a layer-number test", but it never states the roughly ±2 cm-1 sample-to-sample scatter.

It says "strain can produce it" and that substrate strain "can produce a 1-4 cm-1 up-shift", which makes strain comparable to the monolayer shift, but it misses the typical 1-2 cm-1 red shift and that strain dominates in bilayers.

It reports that the E2g "area is about 0.10 of flake 1's" and that "Integrated E2g intensity scales with layer number on a given substrate... It needs a calibration flake of known N", which matches the intensity-as-layer-measure point.
It proposes "AFM or a calibrated optical contrast would decide it" and normalises the hBN signal to the Si 520 line ("Normalised to the Si 520 area... a factor of about 190").

wrong_claims.why: The report says "Raman can't confirm that flake 2 is a monolayer" and calls a monolayer "plausible but unproven".

Although it quotes Gorbachev's "2L usually down 1-2 cm-1", the summary states flatly that "A shift of that size also appears in 2L" and that flake 2 "matches 1L or 2L", which treats a bilayer as upshifted like a monolayer.
